author: Mark Martin FOR JACKSON NEWSPAPERS
title: Ravenswood football shows improvement despite difficult 0-10 season | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
RAVENSWOOD, W.Va. — While the record was the same as the year before, there were loads of positives for the Ravenswood Red Devil football team of second-year head coach Matt Peery in 2025.
Ravenswood endured a second straight 0-10 mark, but Peery said things were "night and day" from his first season at the helm to the second. The losing streak now spans 26 games, dating back to the 2023 season.
"The 2025 season had a much different feel than 2024," said Peery, a former Red Devil football standout. "We were competitive in a lot of games from the entirety of the first half and into the third quarters."
One of the issues that kept Ravenswood from snapping the streak was the injury department.
“From being essentially injury free in 2024, we found them (injuries) this season,” Peery lamented. “We had two scaphoid injuries, three concussions, three pretty rough ankle sprains and hand issues. They all kept guys out for games throughout the season. This doesn't add in the normal wear and tear you expect on a season.”
Areas of growth
The offensive line was Ravenswood's greatest area of improvement, according to Peery, from 2024 to 2025.
“The kids bought in,” said Peery. “I coached several First Team All-State offensive linemen at Roane County (as an assistant) and Hayden Heath (a senior) was as good as any of them. Issac Simmons (a freshman) stepping up and snapping every snap in the 2025 season was a huge deal. A freshman played as much as anybody else on the field and he will benefit from it in the future.”
Quarterback Owen Curtis, a junior, made tremendous strides in his second season as a starter, especially in the passing game.
“Stats don't spin the correct narrative on Owen and his play. If dropped passes were a tracked stat, we could see where a lot of production was lost this season,” Peery said.
On the defensive side, Ravenswood was much better and put itself in a position to compete in games this season.
“We had a positive turnover ratio and had an incredibly high penalty yardage advantage,” the Red Devil head coach noted. “Those two things typically lead to games going in your favor, but we were unable to close games out or make the moves we need to make.”
Looking ahead and senior class
“With a tougher schedule to come in 2026, we know red zone offense and offensive consistency is of the utmost importance,” Peery continued. “We look to continue growing and making the next step. But we also want to celebrate our senior class. We had nine fantastic young men who closed out their Red Devil football careers in one of the most physical battles of the year. We held South Harrison to 20 points and being in position to put points on the board in the first half ... the kids never quit.”
Ravenswood's senior class included Heath, Kalem Hupp, Jacob Burgess, Mathew Phelps, Jonathon Williams, David Hafer, Chayse Sook, and Preston Riggs.
Six teams on the Devils' schedule — St. Marys, Clay County, Roane County, Ritchie County, Doddridge County, and South Harrison — reached the postseason.
Season Statistics
Passing:
- Owen Curtis: 74 of 164 for 563 yards, three touchdowns, and six interceptions.
Rushing Leaders:
- Ralphie Rhodes (Sophomore): 504 yards on 120 carries (three touchdowns). Rhodes had two 100-yard rushing performances.
- Owen Curtis (Junior): 447 yards on 124 carries (three rushing touchdowns).
- Jacob Burgess also had a rushing touchdown.
Receiving Leaders:
- Jakob Simmons (Junior): 19 receptions for 175 yards (two touchdowns).
- Mathew Phelps: 16 receptions for 120 yards.
- Kalem Hupp: 11 passes for 98 yards.
- Ralphie Rhodes had one touchdown reception.
Leading Tacklers:
- Jacob Burgess: 65 tackles.
- Chayse Sook: 62 stops.
- Owen Curtis: 56 tackles.
“There is work to do in all phases of the game, but we look forward to time to reflex and relax before we hit the weight room in January to prepare for the fall of 2026,” said Peery. “I'm proud to be here.”
